Situation1: They join in when the family talks about possible weekend plans.
Expectation2: Challenge unfair systems and influence policy change
Situation2: They gather recurring cases of unfair treatment and bring them to discussions with community leaders or officials.
Story: I sat at the dinner table, my younger sister excitedly waving a brochure for a weekend hiking trip. My parents chimed in, eager for us all to spend time together. I nodded, trying to match their enthusiasm, but my mind kept drifting to the stack of case files in my bag—stories of people in our community facing discrimination, stories I’d promised to bring to the city council meeting scheduled for the same weekend. My family expected me to be present, to laugh and share in the simple joy of being together. But as an advocate, I felt the weight of responsibility to those who had trusted me with their voices, hoping I could help spark change. The two worlds pulled at me, each demanding my full attention, each unwilling to wait. My heart ached as I listened to my sister’s plans, knowing that whatever I chose, I would be letting someone down.
